faults.fault: At 1.6x width the carcass broadens but the front fittings keep their original size: the widened front is mostly blank wood panel each side of an unchanged centre, with the grilles and title-strip block stranded in the middle and the right bubble tube reading as detached from the front face. A wider jukebox must run the grilles, central grille and title-strip panel wider — extra blank panel where those belong is a blocking fault, not a pass.

At 1.5x height the added lower-cabinet area shows vertically streaked, smeared wood grain — dark bands a player could point at. The taller-lower-body idea is correct; the texture feeding it is stretched.

In the solid and wireframe views a flat rectangular slab protrudes beyond the arch at the upper-left of the body — geometry standing clear of the cabinet that should not exist, visible as a step off the silhouette in image 6.

wider_means: A wider jukebox is a broader cabinet: the arched wooden carcass, the speaker grilles, the central grille and the title-strip panel all run wider, with the same single dome and coin door.
taller_means: A taller jukebox has a taller plain wooden lower cabinet body -- more bare wood panel below the control deck and around the grille -- not a bigger dome or taller grille.
